title: Elden Ring
description: Elden Ring is a massive open-world action RPG set in the Lands Between, a dark fantasy world created in collaboration with George R.R. Martin. You play as a Tarnished seeking to restore the Elden Ring and become Elden Lord. Combat is methodical and punishing — every enemy can kill you, and bosses require patience, pattern recognition, and precise timing. The open world is dense with secrets, hidden dungeons, and optional areas. Build variety is enormous: sorcery, faith, strength, dexterity, arcane, or hybrid combinations all feel distinct. The lore is cryptic and environmental, rewarding players who read item descriptions and explore thoroughly.
why_people_love_it: Unmatched sense of discovery and exploration. Every corner of the map hides something. Boss fights feel like genuine achievements. Build experimentation is endlessly rewarding. The open world adds freedom missing from earlier Souls games.
why_people_dislike_it: Extremely punishing for newcomers. Can feel lonely and confusing without a guide. Some late-game areas feel rushed. PvP balance is inconsistent.
best_for: Players who love challenging combat, deep lore, and the satisfaction of overcoming near-impossible bosses. Ideal if you want an RPG where you earn every inch of progress.

title: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt
description: The Witcher 3 is widely considered one of the greatest RPGs ever made. You play as Geralt of Rivia, a monster hunter searching for his adopted daughter Ciri while navigating a war-torn world. The main story is excellent but the side quests are legendary — many side quests are better written than entire games. The world feels lived-in and morally complex; choices have real consequences. Combat is serviceable but not the main draw. The Blood and Wine DLC alone is worth the price of the game.
why_people_love_it: The best side quests in any RPG. Compelling characters, moral ambiguity, and a world that feels genuinely alive. Two massive DLCs add dozens of hours of top-tier content.
why_people_dislike_it: Combat can feel clunky and dated. Early game inventory management is a mess. Performance issues on older hardware.
best_for: RPG fans who prioritize story, characters, and world-building over combat mechanics. Perfect if you want to get lost in a world for 100+ hours.

title: Hollow Knight
description: Hollow Knight is a hand-drawn metroidvania set in the ruins of an ancient insect kingdom. You explore a vast interconnected underground world, fighting through enemies and challenging bosses with tight, precise combat. The atmosphere is melancholic and haunting. Navigation is mostly without handholding — you draw your own map. The lore is deep and cryptic, delivered through environmental storytelling and brief NPC interactions. The base game is massive and DLCs added even more content for free.
why_people_love_it: Incredible atmosphere and world design. Tight, rewarding combat. One of the best value propositions in gaming — massive amount of content for a low price. The sense of discovery when you find a new area is unmatched.
why_people_dislike_it: Can feel directionless without a guide — easy to get lost for hours. Boss rush content in later DLC is extremely punishing. Navigation before unlocking map tools is frustrating.
best_for: Players who loved exploration-focused games and want tight platformer combat. Great entry point into the Souls-like difficulty philosophy without full 3D complexity.

title: Hades
description: Hades is a roguelike where you play as Zagreus, son of Hades, repeatedly attempting to escape the Underworld. The genius of Hades is that dying is part of the narrative — every failed run advances the story and unlocks new dialogue. Combat is fast, fluid, and extremely satisfying, with each weapon and boon combination feeling distinct. The voice acting and writing are exceptional. Even after dozens of hours the game rewards you with new story beats and character interactions.
why_people_love_it: Story that REWARDS failure instead of punishing it. Incredibly satisfying combat with massive build variety. Every run feels fresh. The best use of the roguelike format for narrative.
why_people_dislike_it: Early runs can feel slow before you unlock upgrades. The game doesn't really open up until your first few deaths, which can put off new players.
best_for: Anyone who has ever bounced off a roguelike because dying felt punishing. Also great for players who want satisfying action with a compelling story.

title: Red Dead Redemption 2
description: Red Dead Redemption 2 is arguably the most technically impressive open world ever made. Set in the American frontier of 1899, you play as outlaw Arthur Morgan navigating the decline of the Van der Linde gang. The story is a slow-burn masterpiece about loyalty, mortality, and the death of the Old West. The world is staggeringly detailed — NPCs have full daily routines, wildlife behaves realistically, weather affects gameplay. It demands patience: this is not a fast-paced game. But for players who surrender to its pace, it's a once-in-a-generation experience.
why_people_love_it: The most immersive open world ever created. A story that genuinely moves you. Side characters that feel more real than protagonists in other games. Incredible attention to detail in every system.
why_people_dislike_it: Very slow pacing — some find the opening hours boring. Controls can feel sluggish. Online mode was neglected in favor of GTA Online.
best_for: Players who want to be completely immersed in a world and don't mind a slower pace. Perfect for story lovers who want something cinematic and emotionally resonant.

title: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
description: Breath of the Wild reinvented open-world game design. Set in a ruined version of Hyrule, Link wakes from a 100-year sleep to defeat Calamity Ganon. The world is built around emergent physics and chemistry systems — almost anything you can think of is possible. See a mountain? You can climb it. Too far? Cut down a tree and use it as a bridge. The game gives you near-total freedom from the first hour, and the sense of discovery never fades. Shrines replace traditional dungeons, and the world is packed with secrets.
why_people_love_it: Unparalleled sense of freedom and discovery. Physics sandbox enables endless creative solutions. The world rewards curiosity at every turn. A true 'see that mountain? You can climb it' game.
why_people_dislike_it: Weapon durability system frustrates many players. Traditional dungeons are replaced by smaller shrines, which disappoints classic Zelda fans. Story is thin.
best_for: Players who love exploration and creative problem-solving. Amazing for people who want a game they can play at their own pace with no wrong answers.

title: Cyberpunk 2077
description: Cyberpunk 2077 — after a troubled launch, now regarded as one of the best RPGs of the generation following the 2.0 update and Phantom Liberty DLC. Set in the neon-soaked Night City, you play as V, a mercenary caught up in a conspiracy involving a legendary criminal's digital ghost. The city is the most detailed urban environment in any game. Build variety is excellent: netrunner (hacking), tech, assault, or stealth playstyles all feel distinct. The main story and Phantom Liberty DLC are genuinely exceptional.
why_people_love_it: Night City is the most impressive open world environment ever rendered. Phantom Liberty is one of the best DLCs ever made. Deep RPG systems after the 2.0 overhaul. Keanu Reeves.
why_people_dislike_it: Launch was a disaster (now fixed). Open world activities feel shallow compared to story content. No third-person option.
best_for: Players who want a dense, atmospheric RPG with a gripping story. Play it now — the launch version and the current version are completely different games.

title: Baldur's Gate 3
description: Baldur's Gate 3 is the most ambitious RPG ever made — a faithful D&D 5e adaptation where nearly every decision has consequences. Set in the Forgotten Realms, your party is infected with a mind flayer parasite and must find a cure while being pulled into a conspiracy that could end the world. The reactivity is staggering: the game tracks and responds to hundreds of player decisions. Combat is deep tactical turn-based. Co-op with up to 4 players is exceptional. You can romance companions, play as a villain, or find entirely unexpected solutions to quests.
why_people_love_it: Unmatched player agency — the game reacts to nearly everything. Deep tactical combat with D&D rules. Companion characters are some of the best-written in any RPG. Multiple full playthroughs feel completely different.
why_people_dislike_it: Act 3 feels slightly rushed compared to Acts 1 and 2. Learning the D&D ruleset has a learning curve. Very long — easy to lose 200+ hours.
best_for: RPG fans who want maximum player agency and don't mind long games. Incredible in co-op. A must-play for D&D fans.

title: Stardew Valley
description: Stardew Valley is a farming RPG where you inherit your grandfather's farm and escape the corporate grind to build a new life. Grow crops, raise animals, mine for ore, fish, build relationships with townsfolk, and explore a small dungeon. There is no fail state and no pressure — time flows at your own pace. Made entirely by one developer over 4 years. Wildly charming and deeply replayable. The co-op mode makes it a perfect game to play with a partner or friend.
why_people_love_it: Deeply relaxing with no pressure or fail state. Surprising amount of depth hidden under the cozy surface. Co-op is heartwarming. One developer made this — the dedication shows in every detail.
why_people_dislike_it: Can feel repetitive after the first year. Endgame lacks clear goals. Mining sections feel weaker than farming.
best_for: Anyone who needs a chill game to decompress. Perfect for people new to gaming, couples gaming together, or veterans who want something calming between intense games.

title: Outer Wilds
description: Outer Wilds is impossible to describe without spoiling. You are a new space explorer in a small solar system caught in a 22-minute time loop that always ends in the sun going supernova. The entire game is about exploration and discovery — there are no quest markers, no combat progression, no upgrades. Your only tool is curiosity. Everything you need to finish the game is knowledge you earn by exploring. One of the most emotionally resonant endings in any game. GO IN BLIND.
why_people_love_it: The most unique game experience in years. Pure discovery-driven gameplay that cannot be replicated once you know the secrets. The ending hits harder than most films. A genuine once-in-a-lifetime game experience.
why_people_dislike_it: Very short. Space flight controls have a learning curve. Some find the lack of direction frustrating. Echoes of the Eye DLC is divisive — very different tone.
best_for: Players who want something genuinely different. MUST be played blind with no guides. If you've never played it, stop reading and go play it.

title: Dark Souls III
description: Dark Souls III is the most polished and accessible entry in the Dark Souls trilogy. Combat is fast and aggressive compared to earlier entries. The game is a love letter to FromSoftware's entire catalog — filled with callbacks and references. Level design is exceptional, with areas that interconnect in satisfying ways. Boss fights are cinematic and demanding. The lore about the age of fire, undead curse, and the cycle of light and dark is delivered entirely through item descriptions and environmental storytelling.
why_people_love_it: Best combat in the trilogy. Stunning boss fights. A satisfying endpoint to the Dark Souls saga. PvP invasions and co-op add massive replayability.
why_people_dislike_it: Less interconnected world than Dark Souls 1. Some areas feel like greatest hits compilations rather than original design.
best_for: Players ready to commit to the Souls experience. Better starting point than DS1 for players who want more modern feel before going back.

title: Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice
description: Sekiro is FromSoftware's most skill-dependent game — there are no stats, no build variety, no co-op. It's purely about mastering the posture/parrying combat system. You play as a shinobi in Sengoku-period Japan protecting your young lord. Combat is a rhythm game disguised as a sword fight: deflect attacks in perfect timing to break posture, then deliver a killing blow. The boss fights are the best FromSoftware has ever designed. Beating a major boss in Sekiro feels better than almost anything else in gaming.
why_people_love_it: The most satisfying combat FromSoftware has ever made. Every boss fight is a perfect dance once you learn it. The setting and art direction are stunning.
why_people_dislike_it: Zero build variety — you either like this combat or you don't. No co-op means you're always alone with the difficulty. Some bosses have notorious difficulty spikes.
best_for: Players who want a pure skill test with no crutches. If you love the idea of a perfect parry system and don't mind there being only one 'right' way to play.

title: Disco Elysium
description: Disco Elysium is a detective RPG unlike anything else. You play as a washed-up cop with amnesia investigating a murder in a dying post-revolutionary city. Your skills — 24 of them — are personified voices in your head that comment, argue, and sometimes take control. There is essentially no combat. The game is about talking, investigating, and making choices that reflect your character build. The writing is exceptional — literary, political, funny, and devastating. Your internal dialogue IS the game.
why_people_love_it: The best writing in any video game. Absolute creative freedom in how you roleplay your detective. A game that genuinely challenges you politically and philosophically. Unforgettable characters.
why_people_dislike_it: Almost no combat or action — pure dialogue and exploration. Political themes are heavy-handed for some. Short and linear on replay.
best_for: Players who love story above all else and don't mind a game that's basically an interactive novel. Essential for anyone who considers games an art form.

title: God of War (2018)
description: God of War is a stunning reinvention of the franchise. Kratos and his young son Atreus travel through Norse mythology on a journey that is ostensibly about spreading ashes but is really about a father learning to connect with his son. The entire game is presented as a single unbroken camera shot with no loading screens. Combat is weighty and satisfying, built around the Leviathan Axe. The story is mature, emotionally resonant, and surprises you repeatedly. Ragnarok continues and in many ways surpasses it.
why_people_love_it: One of the best father-son stories in any medium. Stunning technical achievement with the single-shot presentation. Combat feels incredible. The world-building and mythology are excellent.
why_people_dislike_it: Relatively short for an RPG. Some find the collectibles and upgrade systems bloated. Difficulty on higher settings can be frustrating.
similar_games: The Last of Us Part I
best_for: Anyone who wants a cinematic, story-driven experience with satisfying combat. A masterclass in AAA game design.

title: The Last of Us Part I
description: The Last of Us is a post-apocalyptic survival game set 20 years after a fungal infection devastated humanity. You play as Joel, smuggling a teenage girl named Ellie across the country. The gameplay blends stealth, brutal melee combat, and crafting, but the real achievement is the storytelling and character development. Joel and Ellie's relationship is one of the most convincing in any game. The emotional beats hit harder than almost any film. Part I is the remaster of the original with significant visual and gameplay improvements.
why_people_love_it: One of the most emotionally powerful stories in gaming. Characters feel genuinely real. The ending is controversial but unforgettable. Sets the standard for narrative game design.
why_people_dislike_it: Can feel like a cinematic experience with limited player agency. Some gameplay sections feel repetitive. Part II is divisive.
similar_games: The Last of Us Part II
best_for: Story-first players who want a game that feels like an acclaimed prestige TV show or film.

title: Celeste
description: Celeste is a precision platformer about climbing a mountain that serves as a metaphor for anxiety and depression. The gameplay is brutally challenging but completely fair — death resets you instantly to the last checkpoint. The controls are perfect: every death is your fault, every success feels earned. The story deals with mental health themes with surprising sincerity and depth. An Assist Mode lets players customize the difficulty without shame. The soundtrack by Lena Raine is exceptional.
why_people_love_it: Perfect controls — the tightest platformer mechanics of the decade. Emotional story that resonates deeply. The Assist Mode means anyone can experience it. Incredible soundtrack.
why_people_dislike_it: B-side and C-side chapters are brutally hard even for experienced players. Story may be too personal/emotional for some.
best_for: Players who want a challenging platformer that also makes them feel something. Also for anyone interested in games as a medium for emotional storytelling.

title: Minecraft
description: Minecraft is the best-selling game of all time and for good reason — it is a near-infinite sandbox where you can build anything, survive against monsters, explore procedurally generated worlds, or just dig holes. The survival mode has genuine progression: gather resources, craft tools, build shelters, explore caves, fight bosses, reach the End. The creative mode has no limits. Multiplayer servers have built entire civilizations. The modding community has extended the game into almost every genre imaginable.
why_people_love_it: True creative freedom with no limits. Survival mode has satisfying progression. Something for everyone — builders, explorers, fighters, farmers. Multiplayer with friends is timeless.
why_people_dislike_it: Graphics are intentionally simple. Can feel aimless without self-motivation. Caves update added complexity that may overwhelm new players.
best_for: Everyone. Genuinely. Also especially great for younger players or anyone who wants to be creative.

title: Deep Rock Galactic
description: Deep Rock Galactic is the best co-op game of the decade. You are space dwarves mining on hostile alien planets, fighting through procedurally generated caves full of bugs. Four distinct classes (Scout, Driller, Gunner, Engineer) each bring essential tools and weapons. The game is endlessly replayable, constantly updated with seasons, and has one of the best communities in gaming. ROCK AND STONE.
why_people_love_it: The best co-op experience available. Perfect class synergy. Procedural caves mean every mission feels different. Developer has supported it for years with free updates. Welcoming community.
why_people_dislike_it: Solo experience is significantly weaker than co-op. Visual style is sometimes criticized as generic. Progression can feel grindy.
best_for: Anyone with friends who wants a reliable, fun co-op game. One of the best 'play with friends on Friday night' games ever made.

title: Helldivers 2
description: Helldivers 2 is a co-op third-person shooter with a brilliant satirical setting — you are a soldier of Super Earth fighting for Managed Democracy against giant bugs and killer robots. The game is genuinely difficult, requires real teamwork, and friendly fire is always on (meaning you'll accidentally kill teammates constantly). The live service galactic war means the server community collectively fights to capture or lose planets. Developer communication and in-jokes with the community elevated it into a cultural moment in 2024.
why_people_love_it: Hilarious and tense in equal measure. The galactic war creates genuine community investment. Friendly fire makes for incredible shared stories. Constant live updates.
why_people_dislike_it: Server issues at launch (mostly resolved). Balance patches have been controversial. Requires friends to be fully enjoyable.
best_for: Groups of 2–4 friends who want a chaotic, funny co-op experience where things go hilariously wrong.

title: Doom Eternal
description: Doom Eternal is perhaps the most mechanically demanding single-player FPS ever made. You are the Doom Slayer, and you must constantly move, manage resources, and cycle weapons in a near-constant rhythm of controlled aggression. The game forces you to be aggressive — standing still means dying. Every enemy type has a specific counter. The soundtrack by Mick Gordon is legendary. It's a pure, uncompromising test of skill.
why_people_love_it: The most satisfying FPS combat ever designed when it clicks. Incredible soundtrack. A game that rewards mastery more than almost anything else.
why_people_dislike_it: Enormous skill and cognitive demand — not a casual shooter. Some hate the resource management system. Story is ridiculous.
best_for: FPS players who want a challenging single-player game that rewards getting good. Not for people who want to relax with a shooter.

title: Subnautica
description: Subnautica is an underwater survival game where your spaceship crashes on an ocean planet and you must survive, explore, and eventually escape. The ocean is gorgeous and terrifying in equal measure. Shallow areas are colorful and safe; deep areas become increasingly dark, alien, and horrifying. There is no map. You explore with a scanner and your memory. The sense of scale — realizing how deep the ocean goes — is unlike anything in gaming. The story unfolds naturally through exploration.
why_people_love_it: One of the most unique survival games ever made. The deep ocean terror is genuinely affecting. Discovery is constant and rewarding. The base-building is satisfying.
why_people_dislike_it: No map can be genuinely frustrating. Thalassophobia (fear of the deep ocean) makes parts genuinely unplayable for some. Sequel Below Zero is significantly weaker.
best_for: Players who loved the mystery of Outer Wilds and want a survival-focused take. Also amazing for anyone who finds the deep ocean fascinating and/or terrifying.

title: Return of the Obra Dinn
description: Return of the Obra Dinn is a detective puzzle game where you investigate the fate of 60 crew members aboard a ghost ship. You have a magical pocket watch that lets you witness the moment of death of each person. Using these visions and a logbook, you must deduce the fate of every crew member — how they died, what killed them, and their identity. Made by one person in a distinctive 1-bit dithered art style. One of the most satisfying puzzle experiences ever designed.
why_people_love_it: The most satisfying 'aha' moments in any puzzle game. Completely original concept. The moment you solve a chain of deductions is extraordinary. Stunning 1-bit art style.
why_people_dislike_it: Very short. Can be genuinely stumped without any hints system. The 1-bit art style is an acquired taste.
similar_games: The Case of the Golden Idol
best_for: Players who love pure deduction puzzles and want something they've never played before.

title: Terraria
description: Terraria is a 2D sandbox that looks deceptively simple but has some of the deepest content in gaming. You start with basic tools in a procedurally generated world and progress through hundreds of crafting tiers, dozens of bosses, and multiple biomes. The endgame content rivals dedicated action RPGs in difficulty and depth. The developers have added content for free for over a decade. Often called the best game ever made by its passionate fanbase.
why_people_love_it: Incredible depth hidden behind simple presentation. Boss fights are genuinely exciting. Free updates for 10+ years. Co-op is excellent. The best value in gaming.
why_people_dislike_it: Can feel aimless early on — requires external guidance to understand progression. 2D art puts some players off.
best_for: Players who want the depth of Minecraft but with boss fights and action RPG progression.

title: A Plague Tale: Innocence
description: A Plague Tale: Innocence is a linear stealth-adventure game set in 14th century France during the Black Death. You play as Amicia, protecting her younger brother Hugo as they flee the Inquisition through a France overrun with rats. The rat swarms — millions of procedurally animated rats that fill the screen — are a technical marvel. The sibling relationship and story are genuinely moving. Often overlooked in favor of AAA titles, it punches far above its budget.
why_people_love_it: Brilliant sibling relationship and emotional story. The rat mechanics are visually stunning and create genuine tension. A short, focused game that doesn't overstay its welcome.
why_people_dislike_it: Stealth sections can be repetitive. Combat is very limited. Stealth AI is inconsistent.
similar_games: The Last of Us Part I
Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons
best_for: Players who want a cinematic narrative experience that's shorter and less demanding than The Last of Us.

title: Ghost of Tsushima
description: Ghost of Tsushima is an open-world action game set during the Mongol invasion of Japan in 1274. You play as samurai Jin Sakai, who must abandon the honorable samurai code and become a 'Ghost' to save Tsushima. The setting is breathtaking — arguably the most beautiful open world ever rendered. Combat is fluid and satisfying with multiple stances. The guiding wind mechanic (instead of a minimap) is a design innovation worth studying. The Legends multiplayer mode is a free co-op roguelike.
why_people_love_it: The most beautiful open world ever made. Fluid, satisfying samurai combat. The guiding wind is an elegant navigation design. Strong story about tradition vs necessity.
why_people_dislike_it: Open world structure becomes repetitive. Stealth is underdeveloped. Story is predictable.
best_for: Players who want a beautiful, accessible open-world samurai game without Sekiro's punishing difficulty.

title: Slay the Spire
tags: easy to learn hard to master
description: Slay the Spire invented the roguelike deck-builder genre and remains the best example of it. You build a deck of cards from scratch each run, fighting through enemies and choosing from random card rewards. Four characters each have completely different card pools. Ascension levels let you progressively increase difficulty. Every run is different, and the synergy discovery — when a deck suddenly clicks — is deeply satisfying. One of the most replayable games ever made.
why_people_love_it: Perfect genre invention. The deck-building synergy discovery is endlessly satisfying. Quick runs mean easy to play in short sessions. Massive depth behind simple rules.
why_people_dislike_it: High RNG dependency can feel unfair on bad seeds. Single-player only. Limited narrative.
best_for: Players who like strategy games or card games and want something extremely replayable and satisfying.

title: Valheim
description: Valheim is a Viking survival game where you explore a procedurally generated purgatory, build longhouses, fight massive bosses, and eventually reach Valhalla. It's best played co-op with friends — building a base together and venturing into progressively harder biomes is deeply satisfying. The art style is deliberately low-poly but atmospheric. Bosses act as progression gates that unlock new crafting tiers. The building system is surprisingly deep.
why_people_love_it: Perfect co-op survival experience. Boss fights are excellent progression milestones. Building system is deeply satisfying. The Viking atmosphere is perfectly realized.
why_people_dislike_it: Later biomes feel unfinished (still in early access development). Solo experience is slower. Survival mechanics can feel tedious.
best_for: Groups of friends who want a survival game with clear boss-fight progression goals.

title: Inscryption
description: Inscryption is impossible to describe without spoiling. It begins as a dark cabin card game with horror elements and escape-room puzzles. Then it becomes something else entirely. Then something else again. It is one of the most genuinely surprising games ever made, constantly subverting your expectations about what kind of game it is. Made by one person. GO IN BLIND.
why_people_love_it: The most surprising game of 2021. Multiple genuine 'I can't believe this is happening' moments. The card gameplay is excellent even before the meta layers reveal themselves.
why_people_dislike_it: Acts 2 and 3 are weaker than Act 1. The meta elements may alienate players who just wanted the card game.
best_for: Players who love being genuinely surprised and want an experience they'll be thinking about for weeks.

title: Apex Legends
description: Apex Legends is the best battle royale game ever made from a pure gameplay perspective. The movement system — sliding, bunny hopping, wall running — gives it a high skill ceiling that rewards mechanical mastery. Each legend has unique abilities that create distinct team compositions. The ping system (communicate without voice) is the best non-verbal communication system in any multiplayer game. Free to play with cosmetics only.
why_people_love_it: Best gunplay and movement of any battle royale. The ping system is a genuine design innovation. High skill ceiling rewards improvement. Free to play.
why_people_dislike_it: Learning curve is steep — getting stomped early is common. Ranked mode is stressful. Requires squad coordination to compete at higher levels.
best_for: FPS players who want a free competitive game with genuine skill depth. Best with regular friends to squad with.

title: Ori and the Blind Forest
description: Ori and the Blind Forest is a platformer of extraordinary visual beauty and emotional power. You play as Ori, a small guardian spirit, exploring a dying forest to restore light and find your way home. The art direction is painterly and stunning. The opening sequence is one of the most emotionally powerful moments in gaming. Movement abilities are joyful to use. The Definitive Edition adds content and polish. Ori and the Will of the Wisps (sequel) is arguably even better.
why_people_love_it: One of the most visually beautiful games ever made. The opening is genuinely moving. Movement feels magical. The soundtrack is gorgeous.
why_people_dislike_it: Some precision sections are frustrating. Short. The save system (original) could be punishing.
best_for: Players who want a beautiful, emotional platformer that doesn't require masochistic difficulty commitment.
